description.fun: Timburr loves helping out on building sites, always carrying a squared log, and if rain stops the work, it throws a tantrum and swings its log around. As it grows it carries bigger logs, and once it handles one about three times its own size with ease, it's nearly ready to evolve. Its Japanese name, Dokkorer, comes from dokkorasho, a heave-ho grunt.
description.guide: Timburr is a Fighting-type Pokémon that carries a squared log everywhere and helps out on construction sites. It evolves into Gurdurr, and then into Conkeldurr when traded.
description.tagline: A log-lugging building-site helper that sulks on rainy days.

description.fun: Gurdurr trains its muscles by hauling a steel beam around and loves showing them off to Machoke and other Gurdurr; if it can't measure up, it lies low for a while. It's so solidly built that a whole group of wrestlers couldn't budge it. Unlike Timburr it's no good at building, but it excels at demolition, swinging its girder to take buildings down.
description.guide: Gurdurr is the evolved form of Timburr, a muscular Fighting-type Pokémon that carries a steel beam to train. It is skilled at demolition work. It evolves into Conkeldurr when traded.
description.tagline: A girder-swinging show-off with a knack for demolition.

description.fun: Conkeldurr is said to have taught people how to make concrete more than 2,000 years ago, and concrete it mixes is still tougher than ours, even with the same ingredients. It leans on its concrete pillars like walking canes and swings them in battle using centrifugal force rather than brute strength, but when it goes all out, it tosses them aside and pummels foes with its fists. Its name mixes 'concrete' and 'elder'.
description.guide: Conkeldurr is the final form of Timburr, a Fighting-type Pokémon that carries two concrete pillars, using them as canes and weapons. It is said to have taught humans how to make concrete over 2,000 years ago.
description.tagline: The elderly master builder said to have taught us concrete.
